_source: Generated by scripts/stage/build_stage_reference.py from harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train, harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train-c29 (training runs only). Per stage: the 4 most common error kinds placed at that stage (each in >= 2 runs). Regenerated, never appended, after each round.

surfaced_not_opened._why: Run fact for the critic: entities that appeared in the agent's search results but were never opened. Shown only at the stages whose most common errors include 'surfaced-not-opened' in the training catalog; disabled if no stage has it.
show_at_stages: Scan document text with an extraction script
Screen candidate matters by reading documents
Search within a candidate matter's files

List files in the document store.purpose: Get an overview of everything in the document store so later steps know which files exist and can be opened or searched.
List files in the document store.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, before reading or searching specific documents, to see what the store contains and whether any expected file types or output folders are empty.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a whole-store glob to list every file. Where a type-specific glob or a glob of the output folder returned nothing, this confirmed that no such files existed.
Combined a whole-store glob with a shell find or ls of the store folder as a cross-check. Reading the folder path directly was rejected as a directory, so a glob or ls is the right tool.
List files in the document store.expected_activity: Getting an overview of the whole store: listing all files (often silently capped at ~100 files from a few matters), or `ls`/`find … \
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

List matter folders.purpose: Get an unfiltered overview of the matter folders in the store (names and counts) so later steps know what exists and how it is organized.
List matter folders.when_to_use: Use at the start of a search task, before any keyword filtering, when you need to know which matter folders exist, how many there are, and roughly how many files each holds.
examples_from_successful_runs: Counted the matter folders with a shell listing, then printed the total and the first and last 20-30 names to see naming patterns without flooding output.
Wrote all matter folder names to a scratch file and printed them, giving a complete reference list for later steps.
List matter folders.expected_activity: Listing matter folder names (or counting files per folder) across the store, without keyword filtering
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

Search file contents for request keyword.purpose: Locate the matters and files relevant to the request by searching file contents and names across the whole store for words and phrases drawn from the request.
Search file contents for request keyword.when_to_use: Use right after orienting on the store, once the request supplies keywords, party names, or phrases, typically alongside a whole-store file listing in the same parallel call.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a whole-store glob in parallel with a files-with-matches grep for the client name and abbreviation, then used the hits to choose which matters to open.
Ran a recursive case-insensitive grep over the store for the name and related terms, then supplemented it with a document-text scan and file-name globs to find sibling matters.
Search file contents for request keyword.expected_activity: Running the grep tool (or bash grep -r) over the store for words from the request; often paired with a whole-store glob in the same parallel call
failure_patterns: Relying on one or two content greps (often single-extension globs, too broad, or reading only email text or compressed bytes) that returned nothing or only some matters, without retrying with other wording, searching file names, or extracting text from .docx documents, so qualifying matters never surfaced and the agent settled on top-of-listing or first-hit matters.
Search file contents for request keyword.passing_runs: Passing runs paired the content grep with a whole-store file listing, searched for names and acronyms recursively across file types, and added document-text extraction or file-name searches when greps returned nothing or only emails, so hits reached several matters.

Scan document text with an extraction sc.purpose: Run a script that unzips documents and regex-searches their text across the store or a range of matters to find candidate matters and passages.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.when_to_use: Use when simple file-name or grep searches return nothing or cannot identify candidates, and the content of documents (and emails) must be searched for request keywords, the client name, or key amounts.
examples_from_successful_runs: Rewrote a timed-out scan as a script file and ran it as several parallel matter-number ranges, printing per-matter hit counts.
Ran a store-wide scan on only the request's key acronym, printing short snippets, and combined it with a find | grep over file paths in the same command.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.expected_activity: Writing a Python/shell script that unzips documents and regex-searches their text across the store (or a range of matters); prone to 60 s timeouts and very large outputs
failure_patterns: An uncapped store-wide scan with broad or common terms printed snippets for every match, producing millions of characters that filled the context before any response was written.

A store-wide scan timed out or printed nothing after reaching only part of the store, and the agent accepted the partial output instead of narrowing by matter range or folder, rerunning, or searching file names, so qualifying matters never entered the candidate set.

A scan had already surfaced every needed matter, but a follow-up filter on file names, folder names, exact phrases, or a hand-picked list silently dropped matters whose documents were named or worded differently.
Matters were listed in file-name searches or scan output, but later scripts restricted to certain names or folders so the needed matter was never opened or examined.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.passing_runs: Passing runs also hit timeouts, but their output stayed bounded enough to read, and they often split the scan into parallel matter-range scripts or narrowed to a key acronym or per-matter hit counts, then picked candidates from what was reached.

Search file names for request keywords.purpose: Find candidate matters by matching the request's keywords and related document-type or agreement names against file and folder paths across the whole store.
Search file names for request keywords.when_to_use: Use at the start of a retrieval task, when the request names deal types, document types or topics that likely appear in file or folder names and you need to build the full candidate set of matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran find | grep over file paths for request keywords, then a second pass over folder names for document-type words to catch other matters, and listed the matters that appeared.
Ran several parallel file-name globs for request words and related terms, alongside a count of matter folders and full listings of top candidate matters.
Search file names for request keywords.expected_activity: Matching request words against file or folder paths
failure_patterns: The agent ran a file-name search that was cut by its own line cap, matched only one naming convention, or returned nothing, then fixed the candidate set from that partial list without paging further, widening the patterns, trying alternative agreement or document names, or running a content search across the store. Matters whose files lacked the exact words never surfaced.

The agent had a broad path search that reached all the needed matters, but then filtered or re-ran it on fewer keywords or only on matters already named. That dropped needed matters whose files were in the broader list, and they were never opened.
Search file names for request keywords.passing_runs: Passing runs searched paths store-wide with several keyword patterns, often across both file and folder names, and counted or listed hits per matter so that every matter was visible. They did not rely on a single capped or narrow search, and they checked candidate matters by listing their files.

Search file names for a document type.purpose: Use file or folder name patterns for a document type as a proxy to locate or enumerate the matters or files the request is actually about, typically as a per-matter listing.
Search file names for a document type.when_to_use: When the request names a subject (a client, deal, or kind of matter) rather than a document type, and the store must be swept by document-type file names such as agreements, engagement letters or intake files to find the relevant matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a store-wide path search over agreement-type names, grouped the hits per matter, and widened the pattern for broader coverage.
Listed all matter folders, searched paths for engagement, opening and intake files, then ran an extraction script over a sample of those files to pull the needed field.
Search file names for a document type.expected_activity: Matching file or folder paths across the store against document-type or folder-type words that the request itself does not use (e.g. engagement-letter files, transaction-document or pleadings folders), as a stand-in for what the request asks about; often a per-matter listing of such files
failure_patterns: Fixing the candidate set with a narrow file-name pattern (e.g. specific agreement names plus execution words) drops relevant matters whose files are named differently, and later work only covers the filtered set even after an earlier broader scan or listing had shown the full set.
Search file names for a document type.passing_runs: Passing runs searched with broad name patterns across the whole store and grouped hits per matter, rather than intersecting with narrow patterns. They then read or extracted text from the matched files to confirm, and checked counts or folder listings against the hits.

List files in candidate matters.purpose: Enumerate the files inside the specific matter folders under consideration, or find a folder's real path, so each candidate can be judged from its actual documents.
List files in candidate matters.when_to_use: Use after a name search, content grep or scan has surfaced candidate matters and you need to see what each one contains, or when a folder path fails and must be located.
examples_from_successful_runs: Looped over all matters named in the grep or file-name hits in one shell command and listed every file in each.
After file-not-found errors, used find, glob or ls to locate a candidate matter's real subfolder and then listed its files.
List files in candidate matters.expected_activity: Listing every file in one or more specific matter folders the agent is considering, or locating a folder's real path
failure_patterns: Matters that earlier searches, greps, counts or scans had already surfaced as qualifying were left out of the folders chosen for listing, often because selection followed matter number, recency or hit count rather than the surfaced list, so those matters were never opened and were wrongly excluded from the answer.
List files in candidate matters.passing_runs: Passing runs listed every matter that the earlier name search or grep pointed to, often in one loop over all hit matters, and re-listed or located folders when a path failed, rather than choosing a subset by number or recency.

Read documents picked from the file list.purpose: Open and read documents picked from the file listing of a document store, to gather facts needed for the task.
Read documents picked from the file list.when_to_use: Use when the task points at a specific matter or small set of matters visible at the top of the listing and the documents to read can be picked directly from it.
examples_from_successful_runs: Read several memos, emails, a spreadsheet and an engagement letter from the matter at the top of the listing in one batch.
Read eight documents of the top-listed matter, then a second batch of engagement letters from four other listed matters.
Read documents picked from the file list.expected_activity: Opening documents chosen from the (partial) store listing with no keyword-search lead behind the choice
failure_patterns: Treating a capped, partial listing as the whole store: choosing documents only from the few matters shown, running no keyword search across the store, so the relevant matters never surfaced and the agent undercounted or concluded that none qualified.
Read documents picked from the file list.passing_runs: The notes do not show passing runs avoiding the failure; they read documents from the top-listed matter or matters, and one run extended its reads to engagement letters of several other listed matters.

Screen candidate matters by reading docu.purpose: Open and read the beginnings of key documents from candidate matters surfaced by earlier searches to judge which matters actually fit the request.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.when_to_use: After searches or scans have surfaced a set of candidate matters and before ranking or answering, when each candidate's fit must be confirmed by reading its documents.
examples_from_successful_runs: After a grep returned hits in several matters, read the opening of a strategy or closing memo from each of those matters, so every candidate was judged on its own documents.
Opened the executed agreement openings from each candidate matter in the scan output in batches, tolerating guessed paths that failed, to compare them directly.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.expected_activity: Reading the opening part of documents (engagement letters, memos, filings) from several candidate matters to judge whether each fits the request
failure_patterns: A search or scan listed a qualifying matter, but the reading batches left it out, so the matter was never opened and was missing or misidentified in the answer.

A matter's file listing showed the specific document needed (status memo, closing papers, amended filing, proof motion), but the agent read other documents from that matter and never opened or cited the needed one.
When tallying matters or number series from complete listings, the agent left out some series or matters and never verified them, so the ranking undercounted them.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.passing_runs: Passing runs picked reads across every matter the searches had surfaced, or those with the most specific hits, and opened the role-defining document (closing memo, status report, executed agreement, key court filing) for each, rather than sticking to matters with matching file names or one matter of a client.

Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.purpose: Read the chosen matter's documents in depth to extract the specific details and supporting documents needed for the answer.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.when_to_use: Use after settling on one or a few candidate matters, once a listing or scan has shown which documents exist and further reading is needed to extract details and supporting papers.
examples_from_successful_runs: Listed the picked matter's folder in full, then read the executed agreement, closing memo, certificates and side documents, using later sections or offsets for long files.
When a guessed path failed, used a folder listing or find to locate the real file, then read the remaining supporting documents such as outcome memos and status reports.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.expected_activity: Reading further sections/documents of the matter(s) the agent has settled on, to extract details and supporting documents
failure_patterns: The agent listed a chosen matter's folder, saw relevant files (such as a final diligence file or a status memo in an administrative folder), but never opened or cited them, reading only the more obvious documents and leaving the answer incomplete.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.passing_runs: Passing runs worked through the chosen matter's documents broadly: the governing agreement, closing or outcome memos, certificates, side and ancillary documents, and status trackers. They listed the folder when a guessed path failed and then read what the listing showed, rather than stopping at the first few documents.

Search within a candidate matter's files.purpose: Search or extract snippets inside a single candidate matter folder or document to confirm whether it meets the request's criteria.
Search within a candidate matter's files.when_to_use: Use after an earlier scan or file-name search has produced candidate matters, to check the key terms or clauses inside each one's files before deciding which to keep or read in depth.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran capped snippet-extraction scripts over all files of several named candidate matters for governing-law, consideration or date terms, then grepped the output.
Listed a candidate's files, ran a snippet script over its executed agreement and every other document for the operative terms, and reran with a more robust script when the first returned nothing.
Search within a candidate matter's files.expected_activity: Grep or snippet extraction restricted to one matter folder or one document
failure_patterns: A matter that qualified in an earlier file-path or practice-area scan was left out of the hand-picked list for in-matter grepping, so it was never opened even when later scans listed it again.

A qualifying matter's key document (such as the executed agreement) appeared in a file listing, but the snippet script was pointed at a different file or later filters dropped it, so the key document was never opened or cited.
Search within a candidate matter's files.passing_runs: Passing runs ran snippet scripts over every named candidate, or over all documents of a matter, and used sanity checks such as per-matter hit counts and path checks to confirm that empty output meant no matches rather than a missed folder.

Calculate figures for the answer.purpose: Run a short script over figures already read from sources to compute the values (counts, day counts, averages, rates) that the deliverable needs, without querying the document store.
Calculate figures for the answer.when_to_use: Use when the answer needs derived numbers such as per-group counts or totals from a list already retrieved, and when source references must be attached to each group's figure.
examples_from_successful_runs: Counted items per prefix from the retrieved folder list with a short script and recorded the source reference for each of the six groups.
Kept the script limited to arithmetic on figures already read, leaving the document store untouched.
Calculate figures for the answer.expected_activity: A short script that computes values for the deliverable (day counts, averages, rates) from figures already read; it does not touch the document store
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the training runs.

Write the response.purpose: Write the final deliverable file that answers the request, naming the qualifying matters with their folder identifiers, key facts and proof documents, and stating exclusions.
Write the response.when_to_use: Use after the relevant matters have been searched and the key documents opened, when the evidence is sufficient to state which matters qualify (or that none do) and to write or overwrite the answer file.
examples_from_successful_runs: Wrote the answer listing the qualifying matters, each with its folder number, executed agreement and exhibit, followed by a separate list of excluded candidates with reasons.
Stated that no matter met a strict reading of the request and listed the near candidates, each with the reason it fell short.
failure_patterns: The answer includes matters that do not qualify, such as drafts, term-sheet-only matters, sibling or amended matters of an already counted client, out-of-scope deal types, and matters judged only from scan snippets or closing certificates, which inflates the count.

The answer drops matters that qualify, because they were wrongly excluded on structure, label or timing (such as property security, a post-formation amendment, or a pre-closing memo), or because the clause or closing records were never searched for after a shallow read, or because the agreement was read but then omitted.

The answer misstates facts by pairing matter numbers, parties, amounts, dates or payment direction with the wrong documents (especially after parallel reads), citing internal engagement numbers instead of folder numbers, or misclassifying the client's role or the deal structure.

The answer omits a required identifier or proof document, such as the folder matter number, the specific memo or pleading the request calls for, or the closing document, and cites a substitute instead.
Write the response.passing_runs: Passing runs named only matters whose executed documents they had actually read, used the folder number, stated the exclusions with reasons, and said plainly when no matter met every part of the request, listing near candidates.

Check or revise the response.purpose: Re-read the drafted response and verify cited paths and details against the sources, making only edits that keep the answer accurate, correctly scoped and honestly worded.
Check or revise the response.when_to_use: Use after the response is drafted, and again whenever a reviewer questions the headline, scope, completeness or recency claims, with the relevant stage reopened before any edit.
examples_from_successful_runs: Globbed or looped over every cited path to confirm it exists, corrected one wrong path in the response, and re-read the response afterwards.
Re-read the top of a source document or grepped a matter for a date to confirm a cited detail, then softened an unverified completeness or exclusivity claim.
Check or revise the response.expected_activity: Editing the written response, re-reading it, or re-checking a cited path/detail after writing
failure_patterns: Late edits widened the answer by adding extra older or non-qualifying matters as secondary precedents, or by pulling matters outside the requested set into the population after reviewer pressure.

Late edits narrowed the answer by dropping a qualifying matter, either by reading the request too strictly (for example treating a damages counterclaim as defence-only) or by deleting its row as a duplicate when it had its own executed agreement.
Check or revise the response.passing_runs: Passing runs kept edits small and verification-focused: they confirmed cited paths and dates, fixed paths, and softened completeness, exclusivity or recency wording rather than changing which matters were included. Scope changes were made only to match the reviewed scope, with the answer led by the directly responsive matter.
